Class LivenessSentinel

java.lang.Object
shared.liveness.LivenessSentinel
public class LivenessSentinel extends Object
Bidirectional liveness abstraction encapsulating a periodic heartbeat sender and a watchdog. The sender invokes sendHeartbeatAction every sendIntervalMs ms. The watchdog checks every checkIntervalMs ms whether more than timeoutMs ms have elapsed since the last inbound heartbeat; if so, it invokes onTimeoutAction exactly once and stops. Isolated liveness channel: notifyInbound() must be called exclusively by the handlers of dedicated heartbeat messages (e.g. HeartbeatCommand on the server side, HeartbeatMessage on the client side). Application traffic (game states, lobby commands, etc.) does not update the liveness timestamp. This ensures that a stall in application traffic does not mask a dead server/client, and that silence on heartbeats is not compensated by heavy application messaging. Timing invariant: timeoutMs > 2 * sendIntervalMs is required to tolerate scheduling jitter and transient delays caused by large messages that keep the sender busy. With the default values (sendIntervalMs=2s, timeoutMs=10s) the maximum detection time is timeoutMs + checkIntervalMs = 12s. Thread safety: this class is thread-safe. notifyInbound() may be called from any thread at any time at O(1) cost with no lock (volatile field write). start() and stop() are idempotent. Transport agnostic: this class imports nothing from network.*, shared.message.* or shared.command.*. Coupling happens exclusively through the callbacks passed to the constructor.

  • Constructor Details

    • LivenessSentinel

      public LivenessSentinel(String threadNameSuffix, long sendIntervalMs, long checkIntervalMs, long timeoutMs, Runnable sendHeartbeatAction, Runnable onTimeoutAction)
      Constructs a sentinel that is not yet started.
      Parameters:
      threadNameSuffix - suffix used to name the internal thread ("liveness-" + suffix)
      sendIntervalMs - heartbeat send interval in milliseconds
      checkIntervalMs - watchdog check interval in milliseconds
      timeoutMs - silence threshold beyond which the connection is declared dead; must be > 2 * sendIntervalMs
      sendHeartbeatAction - callback invoked periodically to send a heartbeat; exceptions are silenced (the stream may already be closed — the watchdog is the sole arbiter of liveness)
      onTimeoutAction - callback invoked at most once when the watchdog fires; may call stop() on this same sentinel without deadlock, since stop() acquires no internal lock

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start()
      Starts the sender and the watchdog. Idempotent: subsequent calls to start() are no-ops. lastInbound is initialised to the current time at this call.

    • notifyInbound

      public void notifyInbound()
      Notifies the sentinel that an inbound message has arrived, updating the timestamp used by the watchdog. O(1) cost, no lock.

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Stops the sender and the watchdog. Idempotent: uses AtomicBoolean.compareAndSet(boolean, boolean) to guarantee safety on repeated calls.
